record.original_question: Assume that in dimension d+1 the tetrahedral Kontsevich graph flow on a Nambu-Poisson bracket is trivial, meaning the flow Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) can be written as the Schouten bracket [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3})]] for some vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}. Determine whether that trivializing vector field can always be constructed as a linear combination of descendants, in dimension d+1, of the two-dimensional 'sunflower' graph.

evidence.quote: If Ṗ = Q gamma3 d+1(P⊗4) is trivial, Q gamma3 d+1 = [[P, X⃗ gamma3 d+1(P⊗3)]], then is X⃗ gamma3 d+1 found over linear combinations of the 'sunflower' descendants from 2D ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. On $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ with coordinates $(x^1,\dots,x^{d+1})$, a Nambu–Poisson bivector is given by
$$P^{ij}(x) = \varrho(x)\,\varepsilon^{ij i_1\cdots i_{d-1}}\,\partial_{i_1} a_1(x)\cdots \partial_{i_{d-1}} a_{d-1}(x),$$
where $\varrho$ is a density and $a_1,\dots,a_{d-1}$ are Casimirs, and $\varepsilon$ is the totally antisymmetric symbol. The Schouten bracket $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ is the standard Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket on multivector fields, and $P$ is Poisson, $[\![P,P]\!]=0$.

The Kontsevich tetrahedral graph cocycle $\gamma_3$ (the wedge of two tetrahedra in the directed graph complex on four vertices) defines, via Kontsevich's graph orientation morphism, a bivector flow
$$\dot{P} \;=\; Q_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{\otimes 4}),$$
obtained by summing over all admissible decorations of $\gamma_3$ by copies of $P$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$. This flow preserves the Jacobi identity at first order in the deformation parameter.

Assume that on the class of Nambu–Poisson bivectors on $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ the flow is trivial in the second Poisson cohomology, i.e. there exists a vector field $\vec{X}_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{\otimes 3})$, built polynomially from $P$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, such that
$$Q_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{\otimes 4}) \;=\; [\![\,P,\;\vec{X}_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{\otimes 3})\,]\!].$$

In dimension $d+1=2$, the trivializing vector field is provided by the so-called "sunflower" graph $\vec{X}^{2}_{\mathrm{sun}}$. Its $(d+1)$-dimensional descendants are defined as the finite collection of vector-field micro-graphs on $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ obtained by all admissible ways of distributing the derivative edges incident to each $P$-vertex of the sunflower over the $(d-1)$ Casimirs and the density factor $\varrho$ of $P$ in dimension $d+1$.

Question. Decide whether, whenever the trivialization above exists, the trivializing vector field $\vec{X}_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}$ can always be chosen as a linear combination (with constant coefficients) of the $(d+1)$-dimensional descendants of the $2$D sunflower graph.
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph complex and Nambu–Poisson brackets
artifact.status_search_result: The question is one of the open problems in the ongoing program on the action of Kontsevich graphs on Nambu–Poisson brackets. Triviality of the tetrahedral flow has been established for d=2 (Kontsevich, 1996), d=3 (Buring–Kiselev, 2020), and d=4 (2024); whether the trivializing vector field can always be obtained from descendants of the 2D sunflower graph is posed as an open question, with positive evidence in 3D (41 descendants, solutions over 10 of them), but no general proof.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, VI. Open problems
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems including whether trivializing vector fields can be found over linear combinations of sunflower descendants from 2D.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, II. The tetrahedral flow is a coboundary in 4D
status_evidence.snippet: Triviality of the tetrahedral flow established up through dimension 4.
status_evidence.claim: Trivializations are known in low dimensions but the sunflower-descendant ansatz is not known to suffice in general.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, V. Implementation
status_evidence.snippet: In 3D, 41 sunflower descendants exist and solutions are found over 10 of them.
status_evidence.claim: Sunflower descendants suffice in 3D, supporting the conjecture but not proving it.
